title: Streaming microbundle allocator with adaptive KV compression
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a new batch formation heuristic for streaming chat completions that forms compact 'microbundles' of turns across sessions, applies adaptive KV compression to reduce GPU memory pressure, and prioritizes low-latency SLOs for interactive users. Goal is to reduce average GPU memory usage per slot by 20% and P95 latency regressions by <5% while improving throughput for mixed short/long-turn workloads.
background: We observed two recurring issues in streaming traffic: 1) fragmented turn boundaries create many small batches that inefficiently use GPU kernels and KV cache slots; 2) KV cache residency for long-context sessions causes slab fragmentation and eviction churn. Existing batchers focus on turn-clustering or session affinity but do not jointly optimize for KV footprint. Prior tickets investigated KV-aware packing and slab consolidation, but we need a light-weight allocator compatible with streaming (low jitter) and continuous batching.
acceptance_criteria: Microbundle allocator integrated into streaming path behind a feature flag
End-to-end e2e benchmark shows >=15% reduction in steady-state GPU KV memory usage without >5% P95 latency regression
Regression suite for short-turn (<=32 tokens) and long-turn (>=1024 tokens) mixes passes
Telemetry exposes per-bundle KV_bytes, eviction_rate, batch_size_distribution, and latency percentiles
Canary rollout plan documented and Console dashboard for rollout monitoring created
implementation_notes: Approach: group in-flight requests into 'microbundles' (2-8 turns) using a sliding window with configurable max-bundle-latency (default 6ms). Compute a KV_footprint estimate per candidate bundle using token length and cached prefix factors; if footprint exceeds slab threshold, trigger per-bundle lossy compression step: quantize KV embeddings with 4-bit linear compression for older prefixes and preserve recent KV exactly. Maintain per-GPU slab occupancy histogram to prefer bundles that reduce fragmentation. Integrate with existing KV eviction hook to mark compressed blocks for prioritized eviction.

Implement canary config and rollout docs
Benchmark across gpu instance types (A100-40GB, T4, H100) with synthetic chat mixes

2026-02-23 - Incorporated 4-bit linear compressor prototype; initial CUDA kernel prototype showed 2.2x memory reduction for historical prefixes with ~1.8ms overhead per bundle
2026-02-28 - Running canary on staging; telemetry indicates 12% KV memory reduction so far and no regression on P50 latency; P95 needs 1 more tuning iteration
decisions: Use lossy 4-bit linear compression for older KV prefixes rather than full quantization-aware recompile to keep runtime complexity low
Keep recent prefixes uncompressed to preserve quality for interactive completion
Feature flag gating for safe rollback and gradual canary
Fallback to existing batcher when estimated bundle latency exceeds configured threshold
risks: Possible quality regressions for completions that attend to far-back tokens if compression is too aggressive
Compression CPU/CUDA cost could add latency for tiny bundles; need to tune thresholds
Interaction with auto-scaling and slab reservation logic may require infra contract changes
notes_for_QA: QA should run mixed-turn workloads, verify model output quality on selected prompt suite (include evals on long-reference QA tasks), validate telemetry emits per-bundle compression ratio and that evicted compressed blocks are recovered correctly.
